haiku-low.q1: It accepts the valid events and lists rejected ones in the response. It returns 202 only after the raw log confirms the write.
haiku-low.q2: It resends the whole batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s to 5 minutes. It never retries events the collector rejected.
haiku-low.q3: The first copy to claim its event_id in the live dedup state wins. Later copies are dropped and only the winning copy is loaded into events_clean.
haiku-low.q4: Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay, because received_at is server time and the client timestamp is never used for this.
haiku-low.q5: A key-value store keyed by event_id, used only by the live processor, recording the claiming copy's log offset. Claims expire after 8 days.
haiku-low.q7: It commits the offset only after loading, so nothing is lost. Reprocessing can duplicate rows, accepted until the next replay of that day removes them.
haiku-low.q8: The archive files for that day and the 7 days before. Written to a staging table, then atomically swapped into that day's events_clean partition.
haiku-low.q9: Using its own temporary state, it keeps an event only if no copy with a smaller received_at exists, reading the 7 prior days' archive too.
haiku-low.q10: The old partition stays unchanged, since the swap only happens after the count matches. The operator investigates and reruns the job.
haiku-low.q11: Only a closed UTC day: over and past 02:00 UTC the next day, with the archiver committed past the end of that day.
haiku-low.q12: Undecided: product has not chosen whether suspected bots are dropped or kept with a flag. Handling is not built yet.

sonnet.q1: It rejects the malformed events (listed in the response, copied to the reject bucket) and still accepts the rest of the batch. It returns 202 only after the raw log confirms the write of the valid events.
sonnet.q2: It resends the whole batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s to 5 minutes. Mobile SDKs keep unacknowledged events on the device up to 7 days. It never retries events the collector rejected.
sonnet.q3: The first copy (the earliest, by smaller received_at / first to claim the event_id) is kept in the live path; the later copy is dropped. After a replay of a day, only the copy with no earlier-received_at copy is kept. (Live crash-duplicates may briefly appear until replay.)
sonnet.q4: Tuesday's partition and replay, because received_at (server time, 00:10 UTC Tuesday) decides the day; the client timestamp is never used.
sonnet.q5: In a key-value store keyed by event_id, used only by the live processor. Each entry holds the log offset of the copy that claimed it. Claims expire after 8 days.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED. (Clients still get 202 once the raw log write is confirmed, since the collector doesn't use the dedup state, but the document doesn't say what the live processor does when the store is unreachable.)
sonnet.q7: Not lost: the processor commits its offset only after the batch is loaded, so on restart it reprocesses from the committed offset. Double-counting: the dedup claim stores the log offset, and a claim with the same offset means the same event read again, so it is processed (not dropped). However, the document admits an event loaded just before a crash can appear twice in the live day; this is accepted and the next replay of that day removes it.
sonnet.q8: It reads the archive (that day's files plus the 7 days before), never the raw log. Rebuilt events are enriched and written to a staging table, then atomically swapped into that day's partition of events_clean.
sonnet.q9: It reads the archive files for day D and the 7 days before, and using its own temporary state keeps an event only if no copy with a smaller received_at exists. That covers first copies received on earlier days.
sonnet.q10: The old partition stays in place unchanged (the swap is atomic, and also fails if staging row count differs from the kept count). The operator investigates and reruns the job.
sonnet.q11: Only a closed day: a UTC day that is over and past 02:00 UTC the next day, and for which the archiver has committed past the end of that day. Archive files exist for 90 days (lifecycle rule), so replay is implicitly limited to that window, though the document doesn't state this explicitly.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. It is an open question: product hasn't decided whether bots are dropped or kept with a flag; not built yet.
